title: Stream live progress output during Go test runs in Grain CI workflows
body:
## Problem

When the `go` CI job (and other Go test steps in `.grain/workflows/tests.yml`) runs, the `Test` step often produces **no live output at all** for 15–35 minutes until `go test` finishes at the very end.

### Root Cause
1. In `.grain/workflows/tests.yml` (lines 662–678), the `go` job's `Test` step redirects all output of `go test -race -timeout 45m ./...` to a file:
   ```sh
   set +e
   go test -race -timeout 45m ./... > /tmp/gotest.log 2>&1
   status=$?
   ```
   Nothing is written to stdout while `go test` is running; only after `go test` exits does the step run `grep` and `tail` on `/tmp/gotest.log`.
   This redirection was originally added because noisy passing tests (such as `cmd/grain` tests dumping CLI/daemon output to `os.Stdout`) produced >256 KiB of output, causing `pkg/ci/live.go` (`ci.maxStepOutput`) to elide the middle of the step log and lose `--- FAIL:` lines.
2. In single-package or few-package steps (`postgres`, `run-host`, `package-cache`), `go test` without `-v` or `-json` buffers all output for a package until the entire package finishes, leaving the live CI log blank for minutes at a time.

## Changes Required

1. **Stream concise live progress during `go test` while preserving full failure diagnostics at the head of the final output (`.grain/workflows/tests.yml` + helper script in `scripts/`)**:
   - Add a small helper script (e.g., `scripts/run-go-tests.sh` or `go test -json` stream processor) used by `.grain/workflows/tests.yml` (`go`, `postgres`, `run-host`, `package-cache`):
     - While `go test` runs, stream concise live progress lines to stdout as packages/tests progress (e.g., each package completion line `ok` / `FAIL` / `?`, immediate `--- FAIL:` / `panic:` / `WARNING: DATA RACE` notifications, and periodic heartbeat lines every ~15–30s naming which packages or slow tests are still in flight) while capturing the full raw output in `/tmp/gotest.log`.
     - Because ~68 package completion lines and periodic heartbeats total only a few KiB, the live stream stays well below the 256 KiB `ci.maxStepOutput` limit (`pkg/ci/live.go`) and never triggers middle-elision of failure output.
     - When `go test` finishes, print the structured failure summary (`=== failing tests ===`, `=== panics ===`, `=== data races ===`, `=== per-package results ===`, and tail of `/tmp/gotest.log` on failure) and exit with `go test`'s status code.

2. **Tests**:
   - Add unit/deploy tests (e.g. in `tests/deploy/`) verifying the test runner script streams live progress lines incrementally as input arrives, surfaces failing tests/panics/races, stays compact on passing runs, and preserves the exit status.
   - Verify `tests/deploy`'s workflow checks (`TestTheGoJobDeclaresEveryFileItsOwnTestsRead`, etc.) stay green.

title: Collapse task provenance and work tree by default in the task detail pane
body:
## Problem

In the task detail pane (`ui/src/components/DetailOverlay.jsx`), task provenance is currently expanded inline near the top of the task:
- The `.freshness` header bar (`DetailOverlay.jsx:290–416`) renders inline provenance links (`generated from`, `filedBySuiteRun`, `origin`, `securityReviewTask`, `supersedes`, `supersededBy`, `reverts`, `revertedBy`, `portOf`, `portedBy`, `not ported`, `Google Chat space`).
- Below the description (`DetailOverlay.jsx:462`), `<WorkTree t={t} tasks={tasks} onOpenTask={onOpenTask} />` (`ui/src/components/detail/WorkTree.jsx`) renders the full tree of tasks grown out of the same origin (`Work from task 1: ...` and every sibling/child task row) expanded by default. For tasks filed from a long-running console session like Director, this work tree can contain dozens of tasks and pushes the actual task status, CI checks, and timeline far down the page.

## Changes Required

1. **Collapse task provenance and work tree by default (`ui/src/components/DetailOverlay.jsx`, `ui/src/components/detail/WorkTree.jsx`)**:
   - Group a task's provenance details (origin, `generatedFrom`, `filedBySuiteRun`, `supersedes`/`supersededBy`, `reverts`/`revertedBy`, `portOf`/`portedBy`, `noPort`, `googleChatSpace`, and the `<WorkTree />` when present) into a collapsible provenance disclosure that **starts collapsed by default** and can be expanded by the user on click.
   - Keep primary non-provenance items in `.freshness` (such as freshness age and the task's own PR link `t.pullRequest` / `Internal PR`) directly visible, while collapsing the provenance trail and work tree under a compact summary/toggle (e.g., `Provenance` / `Work from ... (done X of Y)` summary line that expands to show the full provenance links and `<TaskTree />` on demand).
   - Reset the expanded state when switching between tasks (`t.id`).

2. **Tests (`ui/src/components/DetailOverlay.test.jsx`, `ui/src/components/detail/WorkTree.test.jsx`)**:
   - Update existing provenance and `WorkTree` tests and add tests verifying that provenance starts collapsed by default, can be expanded by the user to inspect provenance links and the work tree, and renders nothing when a task has no provenance metadata.

title: Display the pending question text and reply box up front on tasks waiting for user input
body:
## Problem

When a non-interactive task is parked in `awaiting_reply` waiting for user input (e.g. after an agent calls `ask_question`), opening the task in `ui/src/components/DetailOverlay.jsx` shows the task's title and full original description at the top, while the actual question the agent asked is down inside the `<Timeline />` as a comment. On the Inbox page (`ui/src/components/InboxPage.jsx`), the user also has to click `Reply` on the row before `<Responder />` fetches and displays the question text.

The specific text of the question should be put right up front on the task so it is immediately visible and easy for the user to read and respond to.

## Changes Required

1. **Put the pending question and reply box up front in `DetailOverlay.jsx` (`ui/src/components/DetailOverlay.jsx`, new `ui/src/components/detail/PendingQuestion.jsx` or similar)**:
   - When a task is waiting for a user reply (`t.state === "awaiting_reply" && !t.interactive && !t.pendingSecret`) and has a question/comment in `t.comments`:
     - Render a prominent callout/card at the top of `.detail-main` (right above or below the title/header, ahead of the long task description and timeline — the same prominent position alerts and `<PendingSecret />` occupy) that displays:
       - A clear heading/label indicating the task is waiting for the user's answer.
       - The full rendered markdown text of the question (the latest comment on `t.comments`, plus any attachments on that comment).
       - An inline reply composer (`TextField` + attachment picker + `Send` button) right inside the card so the user can answer immediately at the top of the task without scrolling to the timeline.
   - Ensure drafted reply text in the card survives background 3-second poll re-renders.

2. **Show the question text up front in Inbox (`ui/src/components/InboxPage.jsx`)**:
   - For tasks in the `awaiting_reply` group in `InboxPage.jsx` (or via the task list / pre-fetched detail), surface the question text directly on the waiting item so the user can read the question immediately without having to click a button first to reveal what is being asked.

3. **Tests (`ui/src/components/DetailOverlay.test.jsx`, `ui/src/components/InboxPage.test.jsx`)**:
   - Add tests verifying that a task in `awaiting_reply` displays the specific question text and reply box up front at the top of the task detail pane, and that submitting a reply posts the comment and updates the task.

title: Hide underlying task for console sessions and fix session restart, cancel, and delete
body:
## Problem

Console sessions (such as Director and any custom sessions in `ConsoleSessionPage.jsx`) are implemented on top of an underlying `model.Task`, but today that implementation detail leaks into the UI and breaks expected session lifecycle operations (restarting, cancelling, and deleting):

1. **The underlying task is visible in the UI (`ui/src/components/ConsoleSessionPage.jsx`)**:
   - The session header shows `task {task.id}` (`ConsoleSessionPage.jsx:495`).
   - The compose toolbar shows `Open the task behind this session` (`href="/tasks/${task.id}"`, lines 563–570) and `Open the chat before this one` (`href="/tasks/${task.continues}"`, lines 574–583).
   - The restart panel mentions `"readable as closed task {task?.id}"` (line 263).

2. **Sometimes you cannot restart the chat (`ui/src/components/ConsoleSessionPage.jsx:236–237`)**:
   - `Start a fresh chat` is gated on `const offerFresh = Boolean(session.crowded) && Boolean(task) && task.state !== "closed";`. Unless `session.crowded` is true (prompt tokens past `model.PromptWarnTokens` or thread cut), the restart button is completely hidden and the user has no way to restart or reset the session from the session UI.
   - There is also no **Cancel / Stop** button in `ConsoleSessionPage.jsx` / `TaskChat.jsx` when a session turn is currently `running` or `queued`, so the user cannot cancel an in-flight turn from the chat view.

3. **Restarting or deleting a session sometimes does not actually reset the session (`pkg/ui/console_sessions.go`, `pkg/orchestrator/consolesessions.go`, `ui/src/components/ConsoleSessionPage.jsx`)**:
   - **Restart delay & handover carryover**: Clicking `Close this chat and start a fresh one` only calls `POST /api/tasks/${task.id}/close`. Until the daemon's 10-second reconcile loop runs `reconcileConsoleSessions`, `Store.TaskIDWithTag` still returns the closed task ID, leaving the UI stuck on the closed task. Furthermore, `fileConsoleSession` (`pkg/orchestrator/consolesessions.go:234`) always copies the previous task's handover summary (`carryConsoleSessionHandover`) onto the replacement task, and does not stop an in-flight run first if the session was running.
   - **Deleting a session leaves its open task behind (`pkg/ui/console_sessions.go:510–529`)**:
     - `DeleteConsoleSession` only deletes the entry from `cfg.ConsoleSessions` and **never stops or closes the session's underlying task**. If a session with the same ID is created again (or if the last session is `"director"`, where `model.ConsoleSessionsOr(cfg.ConsoleSessions)` immediately falls back to `DefaultConsoleSessions()` when the slice becomes empty!), `TaskIDWithTag` re-attaches to the **exact same open task** with the old conversation still intact.

## Changes Required

1. **Make the underlying task invisible for console sessions (`ui/src/components/ConsoleSessionPage.jsx`, `ui/src/App.jsx`)**:
   - Remove `task {task.id}` from the `ConsoleSessionPage` header (`ConsoleSessionPage.jsx:495`).
   - Remove the `Open the task behind this session` and `Open the chat before this one` buttons (`ConsoleSessionPage.jsx:563–583`), and remove task ID references from session copy.
   - If a user navigates to `/tasks/{id}` for a task that backs a console session (`t.consoleSession`), open/redirect to the session view rather than exposing the raw task detail pane.

2. **Add first-class Session Restart/Reset, Cancel/Stop, and proper Delete (`pkg/ui/console_sessions.go`, `pkg/orchestrator/consolesessions.go`, `ui/src/components/ConsoleSessionPage.jsx`, `ui/src/components/TaskChat.jsx`)**:
   - **Cancel / Stop in-flight turn**: When the session's underlying task is `running` or `queued`, show a **Cancel** / **Stop** control in the session chat (`ConsoleSessionPage.jsx` / `TaskChat.jsx`) that stops the active run (`POST /api/console-sessions/{id}/cancel` or `StopTask`) and returns the session to `awaiting_reply` ready for the next message.
   - **Always-available Restart / Reset session (`POST /api/console-sessions/{id}/restart`)**:
     - Always show the **Restart chat** / **Reset session** control in `ConsoleSessionPage.jsx` (regardless of `session.crowded`; when `session.crowded` is true, surface `session.crowdedNote` as a hint/badge).
     - Allow restarting cleanly (stopping any in-flight run, closing the old underlying task, and **synchronously** filing the new session task right in the endpoint so the response returns the new `taskId` immediately without waiting 10s for the reconcile loop).
     - Support resetting completely fresh (without carrying over the old handover when the user resets the session, or let the user choose whether to keep the handover summary on a crowded split vs. full reset).
   - **Fix Delete (`DELETE /api/console-sessions/{id}`)**:
     - When deleting a console session, stop any in-flight run on its task and close the underlying task so its old conversation is never re-attached if a session with that ID is created later.
     - Handle deleting or resetting `"director"` cleanly so `ConsoleSessionsOr` does not silently resurrect the old unclosed task.

3. **Tests**:
   - Add backend tests in `pkg/ui/console_sessions_test.go` and `pkg/orchestrator/consolesessions_test.go` covering session restart (while idle and while running), cancel, and delete (verifying the old task is stopped/closed and a recreated session starts with a fresh conversation).
   - Update `ui/src/components/ConsoleSessionPage.test.jsx` to verify that task IDs/links are not shown and that Restart, Cancel, and Delete controls work in all session states.

title: Prevent frequent handoffs and short session lengths after a session summarizes and hands off
body:
## Problem

After a session summarizes its output and hands off (either via Grain's `write_handover` mechanism in `pkg/orchestrator/conversation.go` or via the underlying agent CLI's context compaction / cross-dispatch session resume), subsequent session segments between handoffs become noticeably short, causing the session to summarize and hand off frequently.

There are two compounding mechanisms behind this:

### 1. `boundThread` in `pkg/orchestrator/conversation.go` never resets the window after a handover is written
- In `pkg/orchestrator/conversation.go` (`commentThreadSection` and `boundThread`, lines 257–372), all comments ever posted on a task are rendered into a single slice and bounded against `maxConversationBytes = 64 << 10` (64 KiB: `headBudget = 21 KiB` and `tailBudget = 43 KiB`).
- Once a task's cumulative comment history crosses 64 KiB (`cut == true`), **`cut` remains `true` on every single subsequent run forever**, because `boundThread` still measures all comments from the beginning of the task rather than measuring comments added *since* the most recent handover (`c.Handover == true`).
- Consequently, `if cut { b.WriteString(handoverRequest(carried != "")) }` fires on **every** dispatch after the initial 64 KiB threshold is crossed—even if only a single short message was added since the last handover—prompting the agent to call `write_handover` again on every run/turn.
- Furthermore, when `relayHandover` (`pkg/orchestrator/finish.go:963`) records a `write_handover` call, it inserts a new `task_comment` row with `Handover: true`. Every handover comment is rendered as part of `rendered` in `commentThreadSection`, so old handover comments accumulate inside the `tailBudget` (43 KiB) window and crowd out actual conversation messages, shrinking the effective tail window further with each handoff.

### 2. Cross-dispatch `ResumeSession` (`SuspendedPreamble`) re-injects the entire assembled prompt into the resumed CLI conversation
- When a task resumes a suspended CLI session across dispatches (`RunConfig.ResumeSession` / `SuspendedPreamble` in `pkg/agent/retry.go`, `pkg/agent/antigravity/resume.go`, `pkg/agent/claude`, `pkg/agent/codex`), the CLI's on-disk session already contains the initial prompt and all prior turns.
- However, `SuspendedPreamble` sends the **entire** full prompt again (30–80+ KiB of system instructions, tool rules, attempt history, and the full 64 KiB `commentThreadSection`) as a new `USER_INPUT` message on every resumed dispatch.
- When `antigravity` (`agy`) compacts its context window into `<CONTEXT_SUMMARY>`, it retains recent `USER_INPUT` messages under `# User Requests` alongside `<summary>`. Because each resumed dispatch injects a massive `USER_INPUT` prompt (and interactive sessions also carry all 30+ eager MCP tool declarations plus untruncated tool outputs up to the MCP output cap), a large fraction of the post-compaction context window is already consumed immediately after a handoff, causing the next compaction/handoff to trigger after only a few turns.

## Proposed Changes

1. **Reset the conversation window at the latest handover in `pkg/orchestrator/conversation.go`**:
   - When a task has one or more handover comments (`c.Handover == true`), use the **latest** handover comment as the summary of all conversation prior to that point, and exclude older/superseded handover comments from the rendered thread.
   - Measure the active tail budget against comments posted *after* the latest handover comment (plus the initial head context and the carried handover summary), so `cut` (and `handoverRequest`) only triggers again once post-handover comments have accumulated another full `tailBudget` (~43 KiB) of conversation.
   - Ensure `write_handover` during long-running interactive `chat` sessions does not spam `task_comment` with redundant handover rows on every turn when the post-handover delta is still small.
2. **Avoid duplicating the full prompt and conversation history on `ResumeSession` (`pkg/agent/retry.go`, `pkg/orchestrator/dispatch.go`)**:
   - Investigate trimming or delta-encoding what is sent after `SuspendedPreamble` when `ResumeSession` succeeds (or only sending new comments/events since the suspended run ended rather than repeating the static instructions and entire 64 KiB conversation history in the new user turn), while keeping the full prompt as the fallback when session resume is refused or lost (`suspendedResumeLostNote`).
3. **Tests**:
   - Add unit tests in `pkg/orchestrator/conversation_test.go` verifying that after a handover comment is recorded, subsequent runs with small incremental comments do not immediately re-trigger `cut = true` / `handoverRequest`, and that superseded handover comments do not consume `tailBudget`.

title: Iteratively find and remove dead code until no more is found
body:
## Goal

Systematically search the repository (`pkg/`, `cmd/`, `ui/src/`) for dead code—unused functions, methods, types, constants, struct fields, unreferenced React components/exports/helpers, orphaned CSS classes, and obsolete compatibility shims—delete what is genuinely unused, and **repeat the pass iteratively until a full pass finds no more dead code**.

## Process

Run iterative passes in a loop until convergence (a pass yields zero new dead-code removals):

1. **Go codebase (`cmd/...`, `pkg/...`)**:
   - Run static analysis and symbol searches (e.g., `staticcheck`, `unused`, `deadcode` if available or via `go tool` / AST / `grep` across `cmd/` and `pkg/`) to identify:
     - Unexported functions, methods, types, vars, and constants with no callers or references.
     - Exported functions, methods, types, constants, and struct fields in internal/domain packages (`pkg/...`) that have zero callers outside their own declaration (or are only tested by a unit test that tests nothing else, where the production symbol itself is completely dead and unreferenced by any binary, CLI command, HTTP handler, or orchestrator flow).
     - Dead parameters, unreachable branches, and leftover migration shims.
2. **Frontend codebase (`ui/src/...`)**:
   - Check every file, exported function/component, hook, and utility in `ui/src/` for actual imports/usages across `ui/src/`.
   - Remove unused components, dead props/handlers, unreferenced helper functions, and orphaned CSS rules.
3. **Iterate until fixed point**:
   - Removing a dead function or component often makes the helpers, types, or tests it exclusively called dead as well.
   - After each removal pass, re-run the dead-code scan across both Go and UI until a complete pass finds **zero** remaining dead symbols.
4. **Verification**:
   - Ensure `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, and the UI build/tests pass cleanly after the final pass.

title: Show waiting status on tasks held back by sandbox or provider quota
body:
## Problem

When a queued task cannot start because of a model connection (`ModelWaitCapability = "model"`), `grantAdmitter` (`pkg/orchestrator/cycle.go:1070`) records a `model.GrantWait` via `Store.SetGrantWait`, and `grantWaitActivity` (`pkg/ui/tasks.go:432`) surfaces `"waiting: <reason>"` on the task row in `TaskList`, in `DetailOverlay`, and in `read_grain_task`.

However, when a queued task (including one an operator explicitly clicked **Run now** on) is waiting on **quota / capacity**—either:
1. **Host sandbox resource quota / worker capacity** (`!limits.Admits(live, merger) || !limits.SandboxAdmits()` in `pkg/dispatch/dispatch.go:484, 535, 592`), or
2. **Provider usage-limit / quota pause** (`PausedFor` in `pkg/dispatch/dispatch.go:349` / `pausedByUsageLimit` in `pkg/orchestrator/cycle.go`),

`dispatch.Cycle` skips the candidate before `grantAdmitter` is ever reached (and at line 535 `if !canWorker && !canMerger && len(directorIDs) == 0 { return out, nil }` exits before inspecting the ready queue at all). As a result, no `GrantWait` is recorded and the task shows no `"waiting: ..."` status in the UI or CLI, leaving the operator with no visibility into why the task (or a **Run now** request) has not started.

## Proposed Changes

1. **Add a quota/capacity wait capability in `pkg/model/model_selection.go` and `pkg/ui/tasks.go`**:
   - Define `QuotaWaitCapability` (e.g. `const QuotaWaitCapability = "quota"` or `"capacity"`) alongside `ModelWaitCapability`, `TeamSetupWaitCapability`, `BranchWaitCapability`, and `PolicyWaitCapability` in `pkg/model/model_selection.go`.
   - Include `QuotaWaitCapability` in `grantWaitActivity` (`pkg/ui/tasks.go:433`) so a `GrantWait` with `Capability: model.QuotaWaitCapability` renders `"waiting: " + wait.Resource` with `BySetup: true` just like `ModelWaitCapability`.

2. **Record and clear quota `GrantWait` in `pkg/dispatch/dispatch.go` / `pkg/orchestrator/cycle.go`**:
   - When a `RunNow` task (`requested` loop in `pkg/dispatch/dispatch.go:479`) or a ready candidate (`allCandidates` in `pkg/dispatch/dispatch.go`) cannot start due to sandbox quota or worker/merger limits (`!limits.Admits(live, merger) || !limits.SandboxAdmits()`):
     - Do not return early at line 535 before recording wait reasons on eligible ready candidates (or record the wait via `SetGrantWait` using `capacityReason(limits, live, merger)` / `limits.SandboxVerdict().Reason`).
   - Similarly, when a task is skipped by `PausedFor` because its model connection's credential is paused on a provider usage/quota limit (`pausedByUsageLimit` in `pkg/orchestrator/cycle.go`), record a `GrantWait` with the usage-limit pause reason (which connection/credential is paused and when the quota window resets).
   - Ensure `clearAdmissionWait` / `StartRun` clears the `QuotaWaitCapability` wait as soon as the task is admitted or starts a run, and avoid unnecessary write churn on `task_grant_wait` across ticks when the wait reason has not changed.

3. **Tests**:
   - Add unit tests in `pkg/dispatch/`, `pkg/orchestrator/`, and `pkg/ui/` verifying that:
     - A queued task (and a `RunNow` task) held back by sandbox CPU/memory/disk budget (`limits.SandboxVerdict()`) or worker/merger quota displays `"waiting: ..."` with the quota reason in `ListTasks` and `GetTask`.
     - A queued task held back by a provider usage-limit quota pause (`PausedFor`) displays `"waiting: ..."` with the quota pause reason.
     - Starting the task clears the wait status.

title: Give agent sandboxes precedence over CI jobs in the shared sandbox budget
body:
## Problem

Agent runs and CI jobs share the same host sandbox resource budget (`model.Budget` / `model.Ledger`), but in practice queued CI jobs completely starve queued agent sandboxes whenever CI is busy:

1. **Event-driven CI admission vs. periodic `dispatch.Cycle` polling**:
   - In `pkg/ci/gate.go` (`SharedGate.Acquire` / `releaser`), every waiting CI job goroutine is subscribed to `g.wake`. The instant any CI sandbox finishes and releases 2–16 vCPUs, `releaser` closes `g.wake` and another waiting CI job immediately claims the freed capacity in `g.take`.
   - Meanwhile, `dispatch.Cycle` (`pkg/dispatch/dispatch.go`) only checks `limits.SandboxAdmits()` on reconcile ticks (every 10s), does not wake when a CI sandbox releases capacity, and does not register any reservation on `model.Ledger` or `SharedGate` when an eligible agent task is refused for want of sandbox capacity.
2. **Large agent sandboxes (`AgentShape`, e.g. 16 vCPU) never get a hole while small CI jobs (2–4 vCPU) are queued**:
   - Inside `SharedGate`, `aheadOf` and `reserving` (`ReserveAfter`) hold released slivers back so a larger higher-priority CI job can accumulate a hole.
   - However, `SharedGate` only ranks `g.waiters` (CI jobs) and knows nothing about waiting agent runs. Even if an operator clicks **Run now** on a queued task, 2-vCPU and 4-vCPU CI jobs continually consume every freed sliver before `AgentShape` (e.g., 16 vCPU) can ever fit.

## Proposed Changes

1. **Give waiting agent sandboxes precedence over queued CI jobs in the shared sandbox budget (`pkg/model/limits.go`, `pkg/ci/gate.go`, `pkg/dispatch/dispatch.go`, `pkg/orchestrator/cycle.go`)**:
   - Track when `dispatch.Cycle` has one or more otherwise-ready, admissible agent tasks (including `RunNow` requests) that are held back solely by the sandbox resource budget (`!limits.SandboxAdmits()`), or allow `dispatch` / `orchestrator` to register its pending agent sandbox demand (`AgentShape`) on `model.Ledger` (or via a callback on `SharedGate`).
   - In `SharedGate.take` (`pkg/ci/gate.go`), when an agent sandbox is waiting for room in the shared budget, hold back new CI job admissions (`WaitForPriority` / `"waiting behind a queued agent sandbox"`) so released capacity accumulates until the waiting agent run(s) fit and are dispatched.
   - **Deadlock safety (`Stuck` preservation)**: Preserve the existing deadlock escape hatch (`SharedGate.Stuck` / `Sole` rule in `pkg/ci/gate.go:614`): if all currently live sandboxes are agent runs that are themselves blocked in `wait_for_checks` waiting on CI, and the remaining free budget cannot fit the waiting agent sandbox until a live agent run finishes its CI checks, do **not** block the CI jobs that those live agent runs are waiting on.
2. **Wake the dispatcher when CI releases sandbox capacity**:
   - When a CI sandbox is released while an agent task is waiting on sandbox budget, trigger `Wake()` on the reconcile loop so `dispatch.Cycle` immediately claims the freed capacity rather than waiting up to 10s for the next poll tick.
3. **Tests**:
   - Add unit tests in `pkg/ci/gate_test.go` and `pkg/dispatch/` / `pkg/orchestrator/` verifying that:
     - When a 16-vCPU agent task is ready and waiting on sandbox budget alongside queued 4-vCPU CI jobs, releasing 4-vCPU CI sandboxes holds capacity for the agent sandbox and wakes dispatch rather than letting queued CI jobs consume the slivers.
     - Once no agent tasks are waiting on sandbox budget (or once the waiting agent tasks are admitted), queued CI jobs resume admission normally.
     - If live agent runs holding the budget are waiting on a CI job (`Stuck`), that CI job is still allowed through so the deployment cannot deadlock.
